newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds finished sharply higher, rebounding from morning weakness as soft U.S. economic data sent U.S. Treasuries surging.
Dealers said guilder paper slavishly tracked German Bunds, which had been weak in the morning ahead of the announcement of a new 30-year Bund.
The June National Association of Purchasing Managers' (NAPM) index, at 55.7 versus a 56.4 forecast, reversed that trend.
At the same time, economists were forecasting no change in U.S. interest rates from the current meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.
Dealers said Dutch bonds followed Bunds, which in turn were pulled higher by Treasuries, but there was little underlying cash activity in guilders.
"Guilders don't have any original thoughts," noted a London based dealer.
He said Bund futures should continue to strengthen, passing through 102.00 on Wednesday, although hedging of the new 6.5 percent July 4, 2027 Bund could limit the ascent.
Another dealer said short sellers tried to force Bunds down in the morning session but they found a floor at 101.43, adding that the focus on Wednesday would be sales of the 2027 Bund.
A trader said institutional clients remained hesistant ahead of U.S. June unemployment data on Thursday, although the FOMC was not expected to opt for a rate hike at its meeting.
He said these accounts were not interested in buying Dutch state loans, with yields near record lows.
"They have problems making up their minds if they should be short on the benchmark or right on the benchmark. No-one wants to be long," the trader said.
